text: Definition 2.1 ( Zhang et al., 2020 ) . A point $\mathbf{x}$ is a $(\delta,\epsilon)$ -Goldstein stationary point of $f$ if $\mathrm{dist}(\mathbf{0},\partial_{\delta}f(\mathbf{x}))\leq\epsilon$ .
Definition 2.2 ( Zhang and Cutkosky, 2024 ) . A point $\mathbf{x}$ is a $(\lambda,\epsilon)$ -stationary point of $f$ if $\mathcal{P}_{\lambda}f(\mathbf{x})\leq\epsilon$ .

Remark 2.3 . Zhang and Cutkosky (2024) included an additional requirement in the definition of $\mathcal{P}_{\lambda}$ that $\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{y}]=\mathbf{x}$ , which we chose not to include for a more direct comparison to Goldstein stationarity. Note that omitting this condition makes the definition easier to satisfy, hence only implies a stronger lower bound.

Theorem 3.1 . For some absolute constant $c>0$ the following holds: For any $L,\Delta,\delta,\epsilon>0$ satisfying $\epsilon\leq c\cdot\min\{L,\delta L^{2}\Delta^{-1},\Delta\delta^{-1}\}$ , there exists an $L$ -Lipschitz function $f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$ , where $d=\Theta({\Delta L^{2}}{\delta^{-1}\epsilon^{-3}})$ , satisfying $f(\mathbf{0})-\inf f\leq\Delta$ , such that for any zero-respecting first-order algorithm, all of its first $T$ iterates are not $(\delta,\epsilon)$ -Goldstein stationary points of $f$ , unless $T\geq c\cdot\frac{\Delta L^{2}}{\delta\epsilon^{3}}~.$

Theorem 3.2 . For some absolute constant $c>0$ the following holds: For any $L,\Delta,\lambda,\epsilon>0$ satisfying $\epsilon\leq c\cdot\min\{L,\Delta^{2/3}\lambda^{1/3},L^{4}\Delta^{-2}\lambda^{-1}\}$ , there exists an $L$ -Lipschitz function $f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$ , where $d=\Theta({\Delta L^{2}\sqrt{\lambda}}{\epsilon^{-7/2}})$ , satisfying $f(\mathbf{0})-\inf f\leq\Delta$ , such that for any zero-respecting first-order algorithm, all of its first $T$ iterates are not $(\lambda,\epsilon)$ -stationary points of $f$ , unless $T\geq c\cdot\frac{\Delta L^{2}\sqrt{\lambda}}{\epsilon^{7/2}}~.$
